subject: Verifying an analytic and Monte Carlo-based simulation

messages.author: 9044165ad6889125
messages.subject: Verifying an analytic and Monte Carlo-based simulation
parts:
Hi folks,

I have an analytic model that I'm trying to verify using the average chi-square = df rule of thumb (i.e., the average chi-square value for x iterations of model-fitting should = the model df when the population and estimating model are the same). I'm running a monte carlo simulation (1000 repetitions). When the population model and estimating model are the same, the average chi-square should equal the degrees of freedom. The model below has 11 degrees of freedom; therefore the chi-square should be 11. I'm not finding that result and I'm trying to diagnose this issue. Perhaps I'm misunderstanding the rule or this is occurring because the population model is a bifactor model...I'm just not sure nor can I explain this result. 

Syntax is below:

# population model
pop <- ' 
  # define two substantive factors with standardized loadings
  c1 =~ 0.570*x1 + 0.632*x2 + 0.744*x3 + 0.543*x4
  c2 =~ 0.570*x5 + 0.632*x6 + 0.744*x7 + 0.543*x8
  
  # define a single ULMC 
  m1 =~ .271*x1 + .316*x2 + .374*x3 + .3000*x4 + .374*x5 + .3000*x6 + .271*x7 + .316*x8 

  # define a relationship linking substantive factors
  c1 ~~ 0.2*c2
  
  # substantive factors standardized
  c1 ~~ 1*c1
  c2 ~~ 1*c2
  
  # method factor standardized
  m1 ~~ 1*m1
  
  # method factors are not correlated with substantive factors
  c1 ~ 0*m1
  c2 ~ 0*m1
   
  # error variances for substantive factors
  x1 ~~ 0.602*x1
  x2 ~~ 0.501*x2
  x3 ~~ 0.307*x3
  x4 ~~ 0.615*x4
  x5 ~~ 0.535*x5
  x6 ~~ 0.511*x6
  x7 ~~ 0.373*x7
  x8 ~~ 0.605*x8
'

# estimating model
est <- ' 
  # define a single ULMC 
  m1 =~ x8 + x7 + x6 + x5 + x4 + x3 + x2 + x1 
  
  # define three substantive factors with standardized loadings
  c2 =~ x5 + x6 + x7 + x8
  c1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4

  # define a relationship linking substantive factors
  c1 ~~ c2
'
fit <- cfa(est, sample.cov = cov, sample.nobs = 100, std.lv = TRUE, orthogonal=TRUE)

# simulation syntax
simOutput_1.100 <- sim(
  nRep = 1000,
  model = est, # estimating model
  n = 100,
  generate = pop, # generating model
  std.lv = TRUE,
  lavaanfun = 'cfa'
)

# check whether chi square = df & check parameters for bias
summary(simOutput_1.100)

Any guidance?

Chris

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Verifying an analytic and Monte Carlo-based simulation
parts: The model below has 11 degrees of freedom; therefore the chi-square should be 11

That is an asymptotic expectation, and your N is only 100, but I wouldn't expect the resulting mean(chi-squared) to differ a lot from its df (which you didn't indicate in your message).  I expect the problem might be that you forgot to specify orthogonal=TRUE in your sim() call, as you specified in your cfa() call.  Inspecting your summaryParam(simOutput_1.100) output should reveal whether you are estimating more factor covariances than intended, and summary(simOutput_1.100) should indicate whether df = 9 or 11.
